clue.text: Piano used in old American quartet, say

indicators.note: the piano's letter is used inside the other pieces, so it goes into them

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

explanation.surface: A piano part appears in a quartet written by an American composer of yesteryear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' puts P inside O + US. 'say' marks the quartet as just one example of the kind of numbered composition meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical composition with a catalogue number, such as a string quartet, is called a work or opus.

clue.text: Sudden raids using force, or otherwise, say

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
taken as written

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged differently, so these letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes surprise attacks carried out with force or by some other method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' looks like part of 'or otherwise' but signals that SAY is rearranged, giving AYS. 'using' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallies into enemy territory, short sudden attacks, are called incursions or forays.

clue.text: Warning liberal after vote, say

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the one before it in the answer

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
a cross, X, is the mark put on a ballot paper to vote
liberal in the sense of generous or plentiful means ample

explanation.surface: Someone issues a caution to a liberal politician after an election.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warning' is the golfer's shout before a drive. The definition 'say' is used in its sense of introducing an instance.
explanation.definitionFit: Say can introduce an instance, exactly like the phrase used before an illustrative case.

clue.text: A separate thing, it appears, in final parts of the main event, say

indicators.note: in places the word it inside the letters gathered from the other words
final parts of means the last letter of each of the following words is taken

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something seems to be a distinct item within the closing stages of the headline contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of 'the main event, say' give ENTY; 'in' puts IT inside, making ENT-IT-Y. 'appears' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is something with its own distinct, independent existence, a discrete thing.

clue.text: Sailor is sight better looking, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase must be spoken to be heard as the answer

parts.note: to sight something is to see it; better looking means fairer

explanation.surface: A mariner is supposedly the one whose vision is improved, or who looks more handsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see fairer', from 'sight' and 'better looking', when spoken matches the answer. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer is someone who travels by sea, a sailor or mariner.

clue.text: Boyfriend taking part of our capital, say

indicators.note: say signals that a district name spoken out loud gives the answer

parts.note: Bow is a district of East London, the capital for a British setter

explanation.surface: A girl's young man moves into a section of the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is an area of East London; 'our capital' is London for a British newspaper. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a male admirer or boyfriend.

clue.text: Isn't commonly in the sea, say

indicators.note: in places the colloquial negative inside the word for the sea

parts.note: the main is a literary word for the open sea
ain't is a common, non-standard form of isn't

explanation.surface: Something is said not to be found, as the vernacular puts it, in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: AINT goes inside MAIN as M-AINT-AIN. 'commonly' marks non-standard speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to assert or declare it, a sense of say.

clue.text: Swiss who painted substance of the human body, say

indicators.note: say tells us the painter's surname is pronounced like another word

parts.note: in Genesis Adam is made from clay, the stuff of the human body

explanation.surface: An artist from Switzerland depicted the material that the human form is built from.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Klee's surname is pronounced like 'clay', the earth from which man was made in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Klee was a Swiss-born painter, a leading figure of modern art.

clue.text: Part of speech given to church, say

parts.note: a pronoun is one of the grammatical parts of speech
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Some grammatical category is handed over to a religious body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to utter or declare something, which is what say means.

clue.text: Unwritten messages from English chap, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a man is spoken to give the post

parts.note: a chap is a male

explanation.surface: Notes that were never set down on paper come from an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwritten' is fair because electronic notes are typed, not handwritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic messages are sent over a network rather than written on paper.

clue.text: Place such as New York or Washington, say

definitions.text: Place such as New York or Washington
definitions.meaning: New York and Washington are both constituent parts of the USA
to say is to declare or express in words

explanation.surface: Someone speaks of somewhere like New York or Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: Both named places are US states as well as cities, which is the fair overlap.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent division of the USA is a state; to state is to declare formally.

clue.text: Fine clue composed about name, say

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for name
composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-crafted crossword clue has been written about someone's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' suggests calm, but it signals rearrangement, giving INFLUECE, which 'about' opens to take N. 'Fine' is fodder, not praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a say in something is to have influence over it.

clue.text: Container for remains that could be ours, say

indicators.note: could be means these letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the urn for remains might one day hold their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges OURS + SAY. 'that' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ossuary is a container or room in which bones of the dead are kept.

clue.text: Academy's recognition for picture from Kokoschka, say

indicators.note: say signals that the painter's first name sounds the same as the award

parts.note: Oskar Kokoschka was an Austrian expressionist painter

explanation.surface: A film award goes to a painting by the Austrian artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picture' suggests a painting but means a film. Oskar, Kokoschka's first name, sounds like the award. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Academy Award statuette given for films is popularly called an Oscar.

clue.text: Subject to tough search, having smuggled alcohol from Canaries, say

parts.note: to run contraband is to smuggle it, so smuggled is ran
sack is an old fortified white wine from Spain or the Canary Islands

explanation.surface: Customs officers search a person thoroughly after finding drink smuggled from the Canaries.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK is a historical fortified wine (Falstaff's favourite), and 'Canary sack' came from the Canary Islands. 'having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack a place is to search it thoroughly and roughly.

clue.text: Ode men composed about fruit for Dr Seuss, say

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters go round the fruit
composed means written or put together afresh, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

explanation.surface: Poets wrote a verse about fruit for the American children's author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges to NOMDEE, which 'about' opens to take the fruit. Dr Seuss was the pen name of Theodor Geisel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Seuss is the pseudonym that Theodor Geisel wrote under, an example of a pen name.

clue.text: Sturdy paper boats, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for vessels is spoken to give the paper

parts.note: craft can mean boats or vessels, singular or plural

explanation.surface: A strong kind of paper is used to make little boats.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of craft in the sense of vessel is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Kraft is strong brown wrapping paper made from sulphate pulp.

clue.text: For a song, the sound made by bird, say

indicators.note: say signals that a bird's call spoken out loud gives the answer

parts.note: a cheep is the short shrill cry of a young bird

explanation.surface: A bird's call is offered as a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a song' suggests music but is the idiom for something bought very cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: Bought for a song is an idiom for bought at a very low price, inexpensively.

clue.text: In sort of steel, workers put in iron, carbon and manganese, say

indicators.note: put in means the workers are placed inside the reworked letters
sort of means a form of, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: men can mean workers, as in management and men

explanation.surface: Workers add iron, carbon and manganese in making a particular kind of steel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges to ELETS, and 'put in' places the workers inside. The first 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron, carbon and manganese are chemical elements, basic substances in the periodic table.

clue.text: Coke and rum originally served in saloon, say

indicators.note: originally means taking what comes at the start of each of those words

explanation.surface: Rum and Coke is served in the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saloon' looks like a bar but is a type of car (a sedan in the US). 'served in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon is a British car body style with a closed boot, called a sedan elsewhere.

clue.text: Fruit in lots of running water, say

indicators.note: say signals that the flowing water word is spoken to give the fruit

parts.note: currents are flows of water in a river or sea

explanation.surface: Fruit floats on fast-flowing streams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Currants are small dried grapes or small berries such as blackcurrants.

clue.text: Smart group among freshmen, say

indicators.note: among says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: There is a clever clique among new university students.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across fresh(MEN SA)y.
explanation.definitionFit: Mensa is the society whose members have a very high IQ, a group of clever people.

clue.text: Animals forming line, the opposite of 17, say

indicators.note: say signals that the two words are spoken to give the animals

parts.note: a row is a line; the answer to 17 means inexpensive, the opposite of which is dear

explanation.surface: Creatures form a line, contrary to what another clue says.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 means inexpensive, so its opposite is DEAR; 'row dear' said aloud gives the deer. 'forming' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe deer are a small European and Asian species of deer, animals.

clue.text: American actor or Scottish singer in royal house, say

definitions.meaning: James ... was an American actor and Rod ... is a Scottish-heritage singer
the ... were the royal house of Scotland, later spelt Stuart

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star or Scottish rocker lives in a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: The three senses share one surname; 'in' is a link between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewart is the surname of actor Jimmy and singer Rod, and of Scotland's royal dynasty.

clue.text: Boyfriend as replacement for Ted, say

indicators.note: replacement here means re-placing, so the letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A new boyfriend comes along to replace Ted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replacement' suggests swapping Ted out, but it means TED and SAY are re-placed, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, someone one goes steady with.

clue.text: A part of one's hair lifted, say

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone raises one lock of their hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns TRESS upwards to SSERT in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to state firmly, which is a strong sense of say.

clue.text: Large pet for Hans Christian Andersen, say

definitions.meaning: a big breed of dog kept as a pet

explanation.surface: A big dog is bought for the Danish storyteller.
explanation.walkthrough: Andersen, the Danish author of fairy tales, is a 'great Dane' read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant dog breed, and Andersen was a great man from Denmark.

clue.text: Old European's impudent behaviour, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word for cheek is spoken to give the ancient people

parts.note: gall means brazen impudence or cheek

explanation.surface: An ancient Continental person is described as cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gaul was an inhabitant of ancient Gaul, roughly modern France, in Europe.

clue.text: Politician starts in this office, ends in another, say

indicators.note: starts in means taking the opening letters of the next two words
ends in means taking the closing letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A politician begins in one government post and finishes in a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party, a politician.

clue.text: Cotton line in front of Jersey, say

indicators.note: in front of means this letter stands before the next piece

parts.note: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, an isle

explanation.surface: A cotton yarn sits in front of a woollen jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' suggests a sweater but is the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, smooth cotton thread, used for stockings.

clue.text: Relaxed in every other part of exam, say

indicators.note: every other part means taking the first, third and so on letters of each word

explanation.surface: A candidate feels calm through alternate sections of the test.
explanation.walkthrough: E-x-A-m and S-a-Y give the letters. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy can mean free from worry or tension, at ease, relaxed.

clue.text: Without any qualifications, say

definitions.meaning: complete, absolute, total, as in a total fool

explanation.surface: Someone speaks despite having no credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'qualifications' suggests diplomas but means reservations.
explanation.definitionFit: Utter as an adjective means absolute; as a verb it means to speak.

clue.text: Limits of main advance restricted Communist leader, say

indicators.note: say signals that the two words are spoken to give the answer

parts.note: tied means restricted or bound; Karl Marx, founder of communism

explanation.surface: Advances by the main forces were restricted by the Communist leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is the sea, so the definition is how far the sea comes in. 'tied Marx' said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidemarks are the lines showing the highest point reached by the sea.
